title: Finite Pretreatment Limits on Sequential Detection of Permanent Effects in Synthetic Control
banked_reason: D0.5.G: paper_score_ceiling 6.7 < 7.4; delivered subfield below field floor, salvageable=false; information-scale bracket lacks matching constants and certified rational-input computation lacks a continuous-data/practical complexity bridge.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived and maximized a finite-sample Gaussian VAR monitoring package, including the profiled full-level information clock, anytime size, learned-nuisance power, same-experiment lower bound, a rational-input certified infimum, and a sharp dynamic GLS risk bound. D0.5.G capped the delivered paper at subfield (6.7 versus the field threshold 7.4) because the upper and lower thresholds do not match and the certified computation result lacks a continuous-data and practical-complexity bridge. The two omitted dependency declarations and one literature comparison remain unresolved; the banked graph is not review-clean or dependency-complete.
tldr: A finite pretreatment panel limits how quickly the permanent no-donor-spillover vector shift \(Y_t(1)-Y_t(0)=\Delta e\), whose treated-coordinate consequence is \(e^\top(Y_t(1)-Y_t(0))=\Delta\), can be detected when the untreated level is unknown, even if monitoring continues forever. The focal object is the exact profiled full-level Gaussian VAR information clock, including the stationary initial level. A simultaneous region learned from intercept-free pretreatment differences is paid for once; its region-infimum likelihood rule has finite-sample probability-of-ever-false-alarm control, and horizon-uniform precision and score perturbation bounds make the learning cost vanish with \(M\). A Neyman--Pearson comparison for the same retained raw-level experiment gives the matching information-scale obstruction. For rationally encoded instances, a CAD-backed directed-rounding scheme terminates, preserves anytime size, and pays the displayed vanishing \(\nu\) information cost; no practical implementation or complexity guarantee is claimed.
gap: Asymptotic efficient-score monitoring for autoregressive and vector-autoregressive parameter changes, anytime-valid synthetic-control ranks, generic sequential profile likelihood, stable-VAR concentration, and dynamic donor weighting are available separately. The checked results do not combine an unknown untreated intercept, every retained raw pretreatment level, a learned heterogeneous Gaussian VAR, finite-sample size and power, and a same-experiment information lower bound.
fill: The project derives the exact clock for the vector shift \(\Delta e\), whose treated-coordinate consequence is \(\Delta\), builds an intercept-free finite-sample nuisance region, proves one-time anytime size, controls the entire profiled score uniformly in horizon, certifies dynamic-control oracle risk, and places the procedure against a full-raw-panel Gaussian lower bound.
